result.text:
Emberline Electricals Ltd (BUY005) is showing real but so far non-terminal stress. Our own ledger snapshot of 2026-08-24 records 6 open invoices with CL01 totalling EUR 324,700, of which INV000379 at EUR 65,400 is 32 days past due and the remaining five invoices (~EUR 259k) are open but not yet due. There is no settled payment history at all, so the trend is recorded as insufficient_history. External signals point the same way: a Metro Business Daily report of 2025-11-09 (NWS0010, severity 4, vendor_payment_delay) has three vendors describing delays of 60 to 100 days against 45-day terms plus part-payments in place of full settlement, with working capital described as stretched, and a later Commerce Wire item of 2026-01-06 (NWS0011, severity 3, capacity_cut) reports the Coventry unit moving from three shifts to one, contract workers not recalled and procurement slowed.

The band is Watch on a score of 37.2, with a PD of 0.2718. The trace is 0.65 x 44.0 (payment, 32 DPD) + 0.35 x 24.5 (news) = 37.2, giving a weighted payment contribution of 28.6 and a weighted news contribution of 8.6; the news leg uses NWS0010 only, whose base of 45.0 decayed to 24.51 at age_days 320. The adjudicator agreed with caveats and flagged this as the weak end of Watch rather than a comfortable pass. Four points sit outside the formula: the EUR 324,700 exposure exceeds the single EUR 300k CL01 limit and the payment component scores only lateness; the 32 DPD reading has no settled baseline and all six invoices concentrate on one client; the 2026-08-24 payment snapshot predates the as-of date implied by the article ages (320 days from 2025-11-09 and 262 days from 2026-01-06), so the worst line may now be beyond 32 DPD; and NWS0011, decayed value 12.16, contributes nothing because only the top-severity article scores, despite being the more recent signal and an escalation from payment delay to operational pullback. Note the adjudicator's own caveat that NWS0011 names "Emberline Inds." and appears matched on the Coventry location and Electrical Equipment segment rather than legal name.

There is one limit line. Adlerhof Trade Credit (CL01, LIM0010) holds a current limit of 300000 against owed of 324700; the recommendation is FREEZE, revised limit 300000, change 0, on the reason that the buyer is already owed at or above the limit so there is nothing left to cut. PD of 0.2718 is above the pd_target of 0.25 and max_liability_binds is false. Expected loss is unchanged by the action at 66047 before and 66047 after — the freeze halts new exposure but does not reduce what is already on the book. Given the limit was last reviewed in Nov 2024, predating the current overdue balance, the underwriter should pull a current aged-debt position and re-underwrite that line before relying on the score.

To lift this file, the practical steps are settlement of INV000379 (EUR 65,400) and of the ~EUR 259k falling due, which would both clear the overdue position and begin building the settled history that is currently absent — with a trend established, the payment raw of 44.0 would no longer rest on a single unbenchmarked datapoint. Bringing total exposure back within the EUR 300k CL01 limit would remove the breach that the score does not capture and give the freeze somewhere to release to. On the news side, the absence of further adverse items would let the decay on NWS0010 (base 45.0, decayed 24.51 at age_days 320) continue to run off rather than be corroborated, and a reversal of the Coventry pullback described in NWS0011 would counter the escalation concern. Confirming whether "Emberline Inds." is in fact this buyer would also settle whether NWS0011 belongs on the file at all.
